title.en: The thief who learned to read

text.en: A young thief meets a trusting man. Does the thief betray him?

The story is by Ruskin Bond. The narrator is Hari Singh, a fifteen-year-old thief who is experienced and fairly successful.
He meets Anil, about twenty-five, watching a wrestling match. Anil seems easy-going, kind and simple.
Hari tells a made-up story, and Anil takes him in as a cook and gives him food and a place.
Anil is a struggling writer. He trusts Hari so much that he lets him look after his things, which makes the theft difficult.
When Anil sells a story and keeps money in his room, Hari decides to steal it and catch the express train to Lucknow.
Hari takes the notes at night but then thinks of Anil's trust and of learning to read and write, which would make him a clever and respected man.
He goes back and quietly slips the notes under the mattress while Anil sleeps.
Next morning Anil says he made some money and will now pay Hari regularly. Hari decides to learn, and trust has changed him.

problem.en: Anil gives Hari a fifty-rupee note on a day. How much will he pay in a 30-day month if he pays daily?

why.en: The story only mentions the first payment; this is practice.

prompt.en: How did trust change Hari Singh?

requiredIdeas.en: He chose to learn to read and write

points.en: Anil trusts him and employs him.
